why: Negotiations over flag borders also seek peace, making the presence of an existing or impending fight decisive.

why.T3-074: The member cannot place on a phone: a concrete participation problem, rather than a question about the event's rules.

why.T3-138: The speaker withholds a side because they belong to both fandoms; they are not refusing a particular request on its merits.

why.T3-095: Members test departure news against its date and an outside source's non-April-Fools label. Nothing shows members staging the departure claim themselves.

why.T3-022: A new Brand is started elsewhere because the previous one was destroyed, and the old site is explicitly abandoned after repeated red attacks.
why.T3-074: Separate passages identify failed registration as a bug and restart the painting because pixels did not register; that setback is not an attack.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Relocation after destruction would omit the separate failure of pixels to register and the restart undertaken to cope with that bug.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1074161 identifies the bug and C0313085 describes restarting after failed registration.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-074; dropping it would lose the technical placing failure, while retaining the central relocation after attacks.

why.T3-045: The dispute rests on who began at this spot and whether the Ladybug builders had abandoned another location. Offers to find another site and arguments about rudeness develop that priority dispute; no settlement or actual yielding is shown.

why.T3-065: The national room sizes, locates and specifies its own flag, including its cross and maintenance needs. The homeland-flag gate carries these acts together; the concern about numbers motivates the smaller flag.

why.T3-149: Repeated proposals seek to stop confrontation with France and other neighbours, so peace-making rather than a border between previously peaceful works leads. This is item-is-a-bag: independent material also supports T3-010 border settlement, T3-011 help sent, T3-024 voluntary restraint, T3-035 space requests, T3-056 joint marks, T3-076 stopping the room's attackers, T3-081 historical-war framing, T3-084 help requested, T3-139 pleas to attackers, T3-150 alliances, T3-151 reciprocal help, T3-170 friendly work mistaken for attack, T3-194 proposals carried between rooms, and T3-195 existing agreements invoked. Each listed additional theme reaches three concepts; smaller strands are not promoted into also_present.

why.T3-059: The speaker tells others to let assimilation happen because the flag is already ruined. This urges abandonment rather than reporting the speaker's own withdrawal.

why.T3-001: Members stage false releases, lawsuits, ship leaks and variants, then play along or reveal them. Those replies remain inside the room's fakes rather than testing external claims. This is item-is-a-bag: T3-032 objections and T3-048 reactions to official jokes each have several distinct concepts, while C0747797 also independently requests an old joke feature's return under T3-100, exceeding three kinds. Only the additional themes reaching the three-concept floor appear in also_present.

why.T3-024: Members explicitly spare the Halo helmet and other art and require conversation before expansion could look like invasion; these are choices to avoid covering neighbours.
why.T3-151: Separate exchanges offer Green Lattice future help for present help and exchange protection of a smaller neighbour for returned pixels.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Voluntarily sparing neighbouring art does not carry the separate offers and acceptance of help in return for help.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0344156 offers Green Lattice later help for immediate assistance; C1165701 and C1007936 exchange protection and returned pixels.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-151; dropping it would lose the reciprocal exchanges while preserving the recurring restraint toward neighbouring art.

why.T3-061: Most passages pursue Dutch territorial gains: annexing the left, colonising westward, taking a share of occupied space and placing the design over the Czech flag. Orange serves the national territory rather than an independent colour cult.
why.T3-006: Other passages directly call attacks on the Void and Goodboye or report wiping Puerto Rico out, without specifying an extension of the Dutch design.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Territorial enlargement does not fully carry the distinct calls to attack named works and the report of erasing Puerto Rico.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0550111 and C1271525 call attacks, while C0308025 reports another flag wiped from the map.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-006; dropping it would lose the explicit destructive attacks while retaining the dominant territorial expansion.

why.T3-005: Alarms, calls to arms, reinforcements, defence and the report of repelling the Void dominate. These are responses to an attack under way, not simply routine upkeep.
why.T3-021: A distinct sequence calls for repairing destroyed NOPE and reports rebuilding and restoration after the damage.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: The fight against the Void does not carry the separate restoration sequence in which destroyed NOPE is rebuilt and declared fixed.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0705317 requests repair, C0371905 reports rebuilding and C0115639 recounts completing those repairs.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-021; dropping it would omit rebuilding after the destruction while preserving the dominant defensive mobilisation.

why.T3-009: Repeated 'we did it' statements mark the room's work as achieved, with admiration and incidental thanks. Discovery, fading-flame wordplay and one regretful account do not displace the achievement-centred reading.

why.T3-018: The exchange identifies the apparent interface as a deliberately drawn start bar with tabs. It decodes a particular canvas image rather than explaining the event or merely naming a neighbour.

why.T3-038: Members begin the Button with a box, build beneath the sign and report letters under construction. The passages carry actual construction and progress rather than merely proposing an emblem.
why.T3-069: The explicit transfer from the lost sign to defending the Button concentrates effort on one of the room's two pieces.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Building and reporting the pieces does not carry the explicit decision to transfer effort away from the lost sign and onto the surviving Button.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0847708 states that the room has transferred to defending the Button after losing the sign.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-069; dropping it would lose the reallocation between pieces while retaining the recurring construction work.
